title: Prisma's env("DATABASE_URL") has no default — a .env.example alone breaks the "no .env required" promise
detail: schema.prisma used url = env("DATABASE_URL") with only apps/web/.env.example committed (real .env gitignored). A fresh `npm install` failed at postinstall with P1012 'Environment variable not found: DATABASE_URL'. Prisma cannot express a default value inline in the schema for an env() call. Fixed by committing a real apps/web/.env with the default file:./dev.db (not a secret — a local SQLite path) and excluding it from .gitignore's blanket .env rule with a negated pattern, keeping .env.example only as documentation. Plan §9's "no .env required" claim is only true if a real .env ships.

title: postinstall db:setup fails on a fresh clone with no migrations yet — prisma migrate deploy applies nothing, doesn't create tables
detail: `prisma migrate deploy` only applies existing migration files under prisma/migrations/ — it does not create an initial migration from schema.prisma the way `migrate dev` does. Running db:setup before any migration existed silently reported 'No pending migrations to apply' and then the seed script failed with P2021 'table does not exist'. Fixed by generating the first migration once with `npx prisma migrate dev --name init --skip-seed`, committing prisma/migrations/, so `migrate deploy` on a fresh clone has something to apply.

title: apps/web's eslint.config.mjs (flat config) silently ignored all files without an explicit `files` glob
detail: ESLint 9 flat config with a plugin/rules block but no `files` key errored 'you are linting "src", but all files matching the glob pattern are ignored' — flat config has no implicit default file-matching the way .eslintrc did. Fixed by adding `files: ['**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}']`. Once files matched, .tsx/.ts syntax then failed to parse (espree can't parse TS/JSX) until @typescript-eslint/parser was wired in as languageOptions.parser with parserOptions.ecmaFeatures.jsx = true.

title: sync.cjs's touched() check can't see files inside a wholly-new, never-staged directory
detail: `git status --short --porcelain` collapses an entirely untracked directory to one line (`?? packages/`) instead of listing files inside it, until at least one `git add` has run. scripts/sync.cjs's touched('packages/scheduling-core/src') substring check — ported unchanged from service-appointment-scheduler/scripts/sync.cjs — therefore reports no debt for edits inside a brand-new package until the directory is staged once. Not a script bug (same behavior in the source repo); worth knowing when verifying the plan §5 acceptance check ("edit a file under packages/scheduling-core/src/ and confirm the hook reports debt") right after scaffolding — stage once first (`git add`), then the check behaves as documented.

title: A branded unique-symbol type with the brand alongside top-level fields does NOT block a same-shape `as X` cast
detail: First FeasibilityGate.Eligibility design put staffId/day/shift at the top level next to the `[ELIGIBILITY_BRAND]` symbol property. `({staffId, day, shift} as Eligibility)` (no `unknown` bridge) compiled without error — caught by the `@ts-expect-error` test itself reporting 'Unused directive'. Root cause: TS's `X as Y` succeeds if X assignable to Y OR Y assignable to X; a branded interface is always a structural subtype of its own unbranded fields (it has everything the plain shape needs, plus the brand), so 'Y assignable to X' trivially holds regardless of the brand — nominal typing via a symbol property does NOT survive when the branded type is a superset-shape of a plausible plain object. Fix: nest all real data INSIDE the symbol-keyed property (`{[BRAND]: {staffId, day, shift}}`) so the branded type's only TOP-LEVEL member is the private symbol — then it shares zero top-level properties with any plain {staffId,...} shape in either direction, and the cast correctly fails to compile. Verified via `tsc --noEmit` before and after (the @ts-expect-error line flipped from 'unused' to consumed).

title: service-appointment-scheduler's shared-kernel AppError had a stray `readonly?: string` property, unrelated to the intended `readonly details?` line
detail: packages/shared-kernel/src/errors/app-error.ts in the source repo declares `readonly?: string` immediately above `readonly details?: ErrorDetails` -- an unused, likely-accidental property (probably a half-finished edit of the details line) that adds a meaningless optional `readonly` field to every AppError subclass. Harmless at runtime but dead/confusing. Fixed during the port into this repo by deleting the stray line; not reported upstream (out of scope) but noted here since the file is otherwise ported byte-for-byte and a future re-sync from the source should NOT reintroduce it.

title: ADR numbering collision when porting shared-kernel: source's ADR-0001 (transaction/CQRS boundary) had to become ADR-0005 here
detail: packages/shared-kernel code (command-bus.ts, tx-scope.ts, cqrs.error.ts, several interfaces) cites its governing ADR by number AND section (ADR-0001 SS2.3/SS2.4 etc.) in the source repo. This repo's ADR-0001-0004 are already taken by the scheduling-algorithm ADRs (constraint enforcement, the algorithm, demand-to-headcount, zero-dependency package) -- ported the transaction-boundary ADR as docs/adr/0005-transaction-retry-boundary.md, preserving its internal section numbers (only the top-level ADR number changed), and did a global sed s/ADR-0001/ADR-0005/ + path rename across every shared-kernel source file that cited it. Lesson: when porting infrastructure code that cites its own ADR by number, check the target repo's ADR sequence FIRST -- a silent number collision would have two unrelated architectural decisions sharing one citation.

title: packages/scheduling-core's package.json pointed main/types straight at TS source -- worked under Vitest, crashed under a real Node require()
detail: package.json had "main": "./src/index.ts" (never built). vitest transpiles TS on the fly so all 80 scheduling-core specs and apps/web's earlier Next.js usage never surfaced the gap. The moment apps/scheduler-api's compiled CommonJS dist/main.js did `require('@scheduler/scheduling-core')` at real runtime, Node tried to literally parse the .ts file as JS and crashed with `SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'Eligibility'` (a `export { type Eligibility }` line). Fixed by giving scheduling-core a real build step matching shared-kernel's pattern: tsconfig gained module/moduleResolution NodeNext + declaration + declarationMap, package.json gained a `build` script (`tsc -p tsconfig.json`) and main/types repointed to `./dist/index.js`/`./dist/index.d.ts`. All 80 specs still green after rebuilding against dist. Lesson: a package consumed only by a TS-native test runner during development can hide a completely broken production build until something requires it as real JS -- verify the actual consumption path (a real `node dist/...`), not just tests, before calling a package 'done'.

title: Dropped @fastify/static from apps/scheduler-api's dependencies while porting -- @nestjs/platform-fastify needs it present even when useStaticAssets() is never called
detail: package.json ported from ../service-appointment-scheduler had @fastify/static listed; it looked unused (no useStaticAssets() call anywhere in this app) so it was left out when trimming dependencies. NestFactory.create with FastifyAdapter throws at boot: 'The "@fastify/static" package is missing. Please, make sure to install it to take advantage of FastifyAdapter.useStaticAssets().' -- platform-fastify's adapter eagerly checks for the package regardless of whether the feature is used. Fixed by adding it back. Lesson: when trimming a ported package.json, an apparently-unused dependency can still be a hard boot-time requirement of a framework adapter -- verify by actually booting the app, not by grepping for call sites.

title: apps/scheduler-api jest config was silently unable to load @scheduler/shared-kernel in any spec that imports it -- missing the .js-extension-strip moduleNameMapper rule shared-kernel's OWN jest config has
detail: shared-kernel's source uses NodeNext-style relative imports (./errors/app-error.js) so its OWN package.json jest config carries a moduleNameMapper rule { "^(\\.{1,2}/.*)\\.js$": "$1" } to strip the extension before ts-jest's classic "node" moduleResolution looks the file up. apps/scheduler-api's jest config maps the PACKAGE specifier (@scheduler/shared-kernel -> its src/index.ts) but never copied that relative-import-stripping rule, so every spec file that transitively imports shared-kernel (prisma-transient-error.spec.ts, http-logging.interceptor.spec.ts, global-exception.filter.spec.ts -- 3 of the app's 5 suites) failed with "Cannot find module './errors/app-error.js'" the whole time; nobody had noticed because Phase C/D verification used node dist/main.js + curl, never `npm test` inside apps/scheduler-api itself. Fixed by adding the same regex rule to apps/scheduler-api/package.json's jest.moduleNameMapper.

title: @fastify/multipart's declare module 'fastify' augmentation (adds .file()/.parts() to FastifyRequest) does not merge into apps/scheduler-api's own FastifyRequest -- two physically different 'fastify' resolutions
detail: @fastify/multipart hoists to the workspace ROOT node_modules, but 'fastify' itself is a nested, non-hoisted copy under apps/scheduler-api/node_modules (Phase C's @nestjs/platform-fastify version-pin fix, see this file's earlier fastify-duplication entry). TypeScript module augmentation merges by resolved FILE PATH, not by version string: @fastify/multipart's own import of FastifyRequest from 'fastify' (resolved from root) and apps/scheduler-api's own import of FastifyRequest from 'fastify' (resolved from its own nested copy) are two different physical .d.ts files even though both report version 5.11.3 -- so req.file() never appears on the typed request. Worked around by hand-typing the augmented shape at the one call site (type MultipartRequest = FastifyRequest & { file(): Promise<MultipartFile | undefined> }, demand.controller.ts) instead of fighting node_modules layout for one method. Re-check if apps/scheduler-api's fastify pin is ever removed -- the augmentation might start working and the manual type becomes redundant, not wrong.

title: A stale generated @prisma/client (from an earlier session/branch) type-errors on fields that ARE in schema.prisma -- 'does not exist in type ...UpdateInput', not a schema problem
detail: Mid-session typecheck of apps/scheduler-api reported deletedAt/parameters/diagnostics as unknown properties on Shift/StaffMember/ScheduleRun update inputs, even though schema.prisma has always declared them. The generated client under node_modules/@prisma/client had gone stale relative to the schema (unrelated npm installs earlier in the session can invalidate it without regenerating). Fixed by re-running `npm run db:generate` (prisma generate) -- typecheck went clean immediately, no code change needed. Lesson: a Prisma type error naming a field that is visibly present in schema.prisma is a stale-client symptom first, a real schema/code bug second -- regenerate before debugging the type error itself.

title: apps/web (SQLite schema) and apps/scheduler-api (PostgreSQL schema) shared ONE generated Prisma client output directory -- whichever ran `prisma generate` last silently overwrote the other, crashing the other app at boot with P1012
detail: Both apps generate into the workspace-hoisted root node_modules/@prisma/client (Prisma's default client output location, never overridden per-app). apps/scheduler-api crashed at boot ("Error validating datasource `db`: the URL must start with the protocol `file:`", errorCode P1012) after `npm install --workspace=@scheduler/web` ran, even though nothing in that command should have touched Postgres config -- the generated client on disk had simply been re-stomped back to apps/web's SQLite shape at some point, and scheduler-api was reading whatever was there. Fixed immediately by re-running `npm run db:generate` in apps/scheduler-api. The PERMANENT fix (not just this incident's workaround) is Phase E's deletion of apps/web/prisma/ entirely -- with only one schema left in the workspace, this class of bug cannot recur. If a THIRD Prisma-schema-owning package is ever added to this workspace, give it its own `generator client { output = "../generated/client" }` rather than trusting the shared default -- this is exactly the kind of two-schemas-one-output-dir trap that bit twice already (this entry and the earlier stale-client gotchas from Phase D, which were probably this same root cause, just not diagnosed at the time).

title: tsconfig.base.json's lib: ["ES2022"] has no DOM types -- fine for the Node-shaped backend packages, but apps/web never had client-side code (an onChange handler, File/FormData) to need HTMLInputElement/File/FormData until this session's api-client.ts + create-schedule-form.tsx, the first real interactive code in the app
detail: `e.target.value` on an <input>'s onChange handler type-errored as 'Property value does not exist on type EventTarget & HTMLInputElement' -- correct symptom for a missing DOM lib despite HTMLInputElement genuinely having .value, because without "DOM" in `lib`, TS's HTMLInputElement/EventTarget declarations aren't the full DOM ones. Every `create-next-app` scaffold sets `lib: ["dom", "dom.iterable", "esnext"]` by default; this app inherited the Node-oriented root tsconfig.base.json instead and the gap was invisible because page.tsx/layout.tsx were pure server-rendered JSX with zero DOM API usage until now. Fixed with a `lib: ["ES2022", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"]` override in apps/web/tsconfig.json specifically (not the shared base -- the backend packages genuinely should not see DOM types).

title: Root .env was gitignored (never force-added) despite apps/web/.env being force-added for the same "zero setup" reason -- docs/09_running_it.md and RUN.md would have documented a false "no .env to create" claim for a fresh clone
detail: The root .gitignore has a bare `.env` line, which git matches at every directory level -- apps/web/.env is tracked anyway because it was explicitly `git add -f`'d early on (its own comment: 'not a secret, a local path, committed deliberately for zero setup'). Root .env, read by apps/scheduler-api (DB_PASSWORD=rootpassword, a throwaway local Docker Postgres credential -- also not a real secret), was never given the same treatment and stayed gitignored. Caught while writing docs/09_running_it.md's quick-start section, which was about to repeat the 'no .env to write' claim without it being true anymore for the two-app shape. Fixed with `git add -f .env` (staged only, matches apps/web/.env's existing precedent) rather than writing docs around an untracked file.

title: scripts/sync.cjs's own Prisma-generate trigger silently kept pointing at apps/web/prisma/ after Phase E deleted it -- the Stop hook would have run `npx prisma generate --schema=apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma` against a path that no longer exists on the next apps/web/prisma-adjacent edit, and nobody would have noticed because the hook only prints to stderr on the harness's Stop event, easy to miss
detail: Phase E deleted apps/web/prisma/ entirely (moved persistence to apps/scheduler-api). scripts/sync.cjs's own `touched('apps/web/prisma/')` trigger and its `--schema=apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma` command were never updated -- this file is TOOLING, not app code, so it wasn't touched by the Phase E deletion sweep (which only looked at apps/web's own contents) and wasn't caught by typecheck/lint/test either, since it's a plain Node script with no compile step. Caught only because Phase F's docs/09_running_it.md told the reader to run `node scripts/sync.cjs` as a verification step, and this session actually ran it (init plan §5's own acceptance rule: 'run them, do not eyeball' -- the exact discipline that would have caught this immediately if applied to sync.cjs itself after Phase E). Fixed: trigger and command retargeted to apps/scheduler-api/prisma/. Lesson: a repo-shape change (delete/move a directory a tooling script hardcodes a path to) needs a grep across scripts/*.cjs and .claude/hooks/*.cjs for that path, not just the app-code sweep -- tooling scripts don't fail typecheck/lint/test when they silently point at nothing.

title: directives/cqrs_pattern.md was referenced by name in 8 real code/doc locations (scheduler-api-repos.ts, scheduling.query-repository.ts, every controller, eslint.config.mjs, docs/adr/0005-*.md) since Phase D, but the file itself never existed -- the original 'not ported, self-explanatory' call in init-source.plan.md was wrong, not just later-superseded
detail: User asked to cross-check which directives should be near-identical across the two scenarios in this collection, since apps/scheduler-api's CQRS mechanism is packages/shared-kernel ported byte-for-byte from ../service-appointment-scheduler -- that mechanism's own directive (cqrs_pattern.md) was never ported alongside it. Every comment pointing at 'directives/cqrs_pattern.md §N' across 8 files had been pointing at nothing for two build phases (D through F) without anyone noticing, because nothing checks that a directive path referenced in a code comment actually resolves to a file -- typecheck/lint/test don't read comments. Found only by a deliberate cross-reference audit (grep for the string 'cqrs_pattern' across the whole repo), not by any automated check. Fixed by porting the file (adapted to this scenario's real entities: SchedulerApiRepos.schedules/staff/shifts/demandCells/assignments/runs, AddAssignmentHandler as the mid-flight-read example instead of booking's availability check), preserving the exact same numbered-subsection structure so every existing section-number reference (§2, §3, §4) in scheduler-api's own code stays correct. Lesson: when porting a mechanism (a bus, a base class, a pattern) from another codebase, grep the destination for every place that will end up referencing ITS DIRECTIVE by name (comments tend to get written assuming the directive already exists) before considering the port done -- the code and the directive drifted apart by two full phases here.

title: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md -- the files auto-loaded at EVERY session start -- still instructed 'Do NOT reintroduce NestJS, Fastify, PostgreSQL, Docker, Turborepo, a CQRS bus; none of it applies here' long after the repo was rebuilt on all six
detail: The backend-architecture reversal (phases A-F) rebuilt this repo on exactly the stack CLAUDE.md's Project Context forbids, and neither entry point was updated -- Phase F's doc reconciliation covered docs/03, docs/09, readme.md, RUN.md but never opened AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, because the plan's Phase F line item listed docs by name and those two files aren't in docs/. Also stale in the same two files: Hard Rules pointed at `src/server/repositories/` (deleted in Phase E), said 'Zod at the route boundary' (route handlers deleted, it's ZodValidationPipe at a NestJS controller now), and said 'no orchestrator' (Turborepo has been the orchestrator since Phase A). This is the highest-impact staleness class in the repo: CLAUDE.md is injected into every session as authoritative instruction, so a wrong Hard Rule actively misdirects the next agent rather than merely being out of date -- and I read this exact file at the start of this session without catching the contradiction, while building on the very stack it forbids. Lesson: when a plan phase says 'reconcile the docs', enumerate EVERY file that asserts architecture (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/00, docs/02, docs/04's header, directives/testing_standard.md, sample-data/README.md), not just the docs/NN_*.md the plan happened to name -- grep for the old stack's nouns instead of trusting the plan's file list.

title: The _templates/ folder I created to PREVENT referenced-but-missing docs was itself full of them — ~34 scenario-local citations (plan §N, ADR-000N, assumption N, backend-architecture-reversal.plan.md) that would dangle in any new scenario
detail: Built the templates by copying scenario 02's specialized directives, which carried every scenario-local citation with them: `.ai/plans/backend-architecture-reversal.plan.md §4/§6`, `docs/adr/0005-transaction-retry-boundary.md`, `ADR-0001`/`ADR-0004`, `plan §0.1/§2.1/§2.2/§4/§7/§7.4/§7.6/§8/§8.1`, `assumption 10/11/12/14`. None of those exist in a scenario 03, so the folder whose entire stated purpose is preventing 'a directive path that resolves to nothing' would have shipped exactly that bug into every future scenario — the same failure it documents in its own README. Fixed with two reviewed replacement passes (explicit from→to pairs, never a blind regex over prose): citations became generic forms ('the scenario's transaction/retry-boundary ADR', 'the dependency-free core package'), and a third pass caught scenario-02 facts stated as universal rules (a specific Vitest/Jest package split, a frontend's NEXT_PUBLIC_ env var, the API port 4102, 'every handler built in Phase D'). Deliberately KEPT concrete: domain examples like FeasibilityGate/SchedulerApiRepos/the scheduling module — leaving one un-swapped is merely unspecialized, whereas a dangling citation or a wrong command is actively broken. That distinction is now the documented rule for when to use {{PLACEHOLDER}} vs a concrete example. Lesson: a template derived from a working copy inherits that copy's entire reference graph — grep the template for every path/section/number citation before calling it reusable.

title: Three docstrings (shift.entity.ts, create-schedule.handler.ts, SchedulesController.create) claimed CreateScheduleHandler seeds the two default shifts -- it doesn't, but the seeding IS real, one layer down in PrismaScheduleRepository.create()
detail: Building the Phase 3 UI plan, I read CreateScheduleHandler's body (`return tx.schedules.create(...)`), saw no shift-seeding code, and concluded (matching three docstrings that agreed with each other) that schedules created through the API ship with 0 shifts -- a real bug, planned a fix (loop over DEFAULT_SHIFTS in the handler), and started implementing it. Before committing, traced the actual call chain one level further: `tx.schedules` is `PrismaScheduleRepository` (scheduler-api-repos.factory.ts), and ITS `create()` already does `shifts: { create: DEFAULT_SHIFTS.map(...) }` as a nested Prisma write -- seeding was real all along, just implemented in the repository rather than the handler the docstrings pointed at. My fix would have silently double-seeded every new schedule to 4 shifts instead of 2. Caught only because I ran `git diff` on the change before moving on and re-read the full call chain (factory -> concrete repository) rather than trusting the handler file's docstring plus its own literal body. Lesson: when three independent docstrings all describe the SAME behavior for a piece of code that plainly doesn't do it, treat that as a signal to trace the actual call chain (interface -> concrete implementation, not just the file with the interesting-looking comment) before concluding it's a bug -- comments describing 'what this achieves' are sometimes true about the call graph, not the file.

title: @fastify/cors v11's own default `methods` is 'GET,HEAD,POST' -- narrower than the popular `cors` npm package's default (GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE) -- silently blocked every PATCH/DELETE route from any real browser via CORS preflight since Phase C, invisible to curl/Swagger since neither goes through CORS
detail: `fastify.register(cors, { origin, credentials })` never set `methods` explicitly, relying on the plugin's default -- assumed (wrongly, without checking) to match the `cors` npm package everyone is more familiar with. Confirmed via `curl -X OPTIONS ... -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: DELETE'`: `access-control-allow-methods: GET,HEAD,POST` in the response, no DELETE/PATCH/PUT at all. Every staff/shift/schedule PATCH and every staff/shift/roster-assignment DELETE has been silently broken for any real browser client since the CORS registration was written (Phase C) -- nobody noticed because Phase C-F verification exclusively used curl (bypasses CORS entirely, no preflight) and Swagger UI (same-origin, no CORS). apps/web (Phase 3) is the first real cross-origin caller these routes ever had. Fixed by setting `methods: ['GET','HEAD','POST','PUT','PATCH','DELETE']` explicitly on the cors registration, with a comment explaining why the default couldn't be trusted. Lesson: never assume a plugin's default matches a similarly-named plugin's default (fastify/cors vs expressjs/cors) -- check with a raw curl OPTIONS preflight, not just that requests succeed via a same-origin or CORS-bypassing client.

title: packages/scheduling-core's ESLint config was missing tsconfigRootDir, and its build tsconfig excluded spec files that the eslint file glob still matched -- two separate causes of the same 'TSConfig does not include this file' parsing error
detail: User's editor showed a red squiggly on index.ts (a file that lints clean on the CLI) with 'TSConfig does not include this file'. Root cause 1: packages/scheduling-core/eslint.config.js was the only one of the 4 workspace ESLint configs (apps/scheduler-api, packages/shared-kernel both have it) missing `tsconfigRootDir: import.meta.dirname` in parserOptions. Without it, a relative `project: './tsconfig.json'` resolves against whatever CWD the ESLint PROCESS has -- correct via `npm run lint --workspace=...` (npm cds into the package first) but wrong from a VS Code ESLint extension whose CWD is the multi-root workspace, silently pointing at a different (or no) tsconfig.json and producing this exact error only in the editor, never the CLI. Fixed by adding tsconfigRootDir, matching the other 3 configs. Root cause 2 (a REAL bug, reproduced on the CLI too): scheduling-core's tsconfig.json deliberately excludes *.spec.ts/*.prop-spec.ts (so `dist/` stays test-free), but eslint.config.js's `files: ['src/**/*.ts']` glob still matches them -- so type-aware linting asked for type info on a file that project genuinely does not include, failing on all 11 spec files package-wide, not an editor artifact. Fixed by adding tsconfig.eslint.json (extends tsconfig.json, re-includes everything under src via exclude: []) used ONLY by eslint's parserOptions.project -- `tsc -p` build/typecheck scripts keep using the original tsconfig.json unchanged, so dist/ still never gets spec files. Recognize this class of bug by: CLI lint is clean but editor is red -> missing tsconfigRootDir; CLI lint ALSO fails on files a tsconfig's exclude list names -> eslint's file glob and the linted tsconfig's include/exclude have drifted apart, needs a separate lint-only tsconfig.
